analysis.title: DeskTalk - Mapping the US data center buildout
key_insights: Data center development has become the latest constraint on the AI trade. Democratic midterm gains in key states point to a slowdown and higher project costs rather than a complete halt to the build-out.
Citi says this does not invalidate the AI selloff, because stretched valuations and elevated capex remain legitimate concerns.
Markets worry that sweeping Democratic wins could embolden a firmer stance on data centers. Public dissatisfaction runs deep as well, not only at the Congress level.
Fifty local measures were on the ballot on Nov 3, and voters approved almost every moratorium under consideration.
Ohio saw the strongest pushback, with at least 14 municipalities adopting bans or restrictions, including Sunbury, the proposed site of a $2bn Amazon project.
There are 300 local data center pauses recorded in 36 states, with Ohio holding the largest concentration of moratoriums.
Current proposals focus on consumer welfare: protecting against higher electricity costs and increasing transparency on energy and water use. They differ on how to manage growth.
Citi lists four indicators to watch: grandfathering of approved projects, megawatts of capacity affected, durability of moratoriums, and hyperscaler capex guidance.
Citi's US CETS are not dip-buyers yet and expect elevated headline risk on the AI infrastructure cycle in the coming days.

Citi Global Equity Strategy downgraded US, global and European tech to Neutral from Overweight. Fundamentals remain attractive, but positioning could move further into net short territory, and Citi would wait for cleaner positioning before returning to Overweight.

market_movers.rationale: Sunbury, Ohio, the proposed site of a $2bn Amazon data center project, adopted a local restriction on the Nov 3 ballot.
CoreWeave's CEO wrote to Texas Governor-elect Hinojosa offering to help shape standards for future data center development.

sector_views.rationale: Global Equity Strategy downgraded US, global and European tech to Neutral from Overweight. Fundamentals remain attractive, but positioning could adjust further into net short territory.

risk_factors: Local moratoriums on data centers could slow the build-out and raise project costs.
Hyperscaler capex commentary indicating constrained capacity or power would imply slowing demand.
Stretched valuations and elevated capex remain concerns for the AI trade.
Further local ballot measures and state-level action beyond Ohio could widen the restrictions.

Citi would wait for cleaner positioning before returning to its Overweight call on tech.
US CETS are not dip-buyers yet and expect elevated headline risk on the AI infrastructure cycle in the coming days.

tension_points.bull_case: Moratoriums are mostly temporary, lasting one or two years, and proposals aim to manage growth and costs rather than halt the build-out completely. Citi says fundamentals remain attractive.
tension_points.bear_case: 300 local pauses across 36 states, near-unanimous approval of ballot moratoriums, and a possible firmer Democratic stance could slow projects and raise costs. Stretched valuations and elevated capex remain concerns.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Any shift in hyperscaler capex commentary that indicates constrained capacity or power would imply slowing demand.
